criteria.method_definition: Discounted purchase, installation, energy, water, consumables, maintenance, successful and failed repairs, downtime assumptions, rework and end-of-life on a declared useful-service profile.
P90 elapsed time from triage to verified restoration including parts waits, travel, failed attempts and rework; also preserve hands-on time separately.
Rate of declared repair tasks restored and post-checked on the first visit, with task mix and sample size disclosed.
Calibrated electrical energy per load that passes the frozen cleaning, rinsing and spin-drying floors; not evaluated when core function gate fails.
Measured water per load that passes the frozen cleaning, rinsing and spin-drying floors, with load and supply conditions declared.
Mass of parts and assemblies actually discarded for a defined repair, with refurbishment/reuse and unknown masses tracked separately.
Observed failures or rework attributable to added connectors, seals, access panels or interfaces under a declared exposure denominator and follow-up window.
Share of accepted exact-fit parts orders physically delivered within a target window in the named market; cancellations, substitutions and incomplete orders remain separate.

rules: Before product comparison, freeze control selection, workloads, method and instrument capability.
Run a control-only pilot to estimate repeatability and measurement uncertainty before candidate measurements.
Do not compare candidates when any hard safety, core function, durability or conformity gate is unknown.
Select the next experiment using decision relevance, cost, risk, expected uncertainty reduction and model sensitivity.
If robust Pareto bounds overlap, record an unresolved trade-off and measure the criterion most likely to change the architecture decision.
next_experiment_policy.existing_information_value_owner: Use the existing Symthaea finite-hypothesis EIG/EVSI kernel and appliance adapter; do not create a parallel information-value scorer.

stakeholder_profiles.context: Household owners and intended users with varied repair confidence, time, budgets and access to local service.
stakeholder_profiles.primary_question: Can the owner use and maintain the appliance safely and affordably without specialist access or hidden service dependencies?
stakeholder_profiles.required_task_boundary: Only intended normal-user maintenance and safe referral/troubleshooting tasks; no opening internal mains, heater, drive, heavy rotating, stored-energy or refrigerant systems.

requirements.rationale: Owner cash affordability depends on local price, tariffs, service availability and declared lifetime; no universal cutoff is assumed.
requirements.evidence_needed: Participant interviews and a transparent local-currency lifecycle model with sensitivity analysis.

requirements.rationale: Acceptable outage depends on household needs and replacement access; threshold must be elicited, not guessed.
requirements.evidence_needed: Contextual user research and named outage scenarios.

requirements.rationale: Efficiency is useful only when cleaning, rinsing and spin-drying floors pass.
requirements.evidence_needed: Frozen matched-load performance protocol with calibrated energy measurement.

requirements.rationale: Water constraints and tariffs vary by location; use a declared successful load as denominator.
requirements.evidence_needed: Frozen load profile, metered water use and local context.

stakeholder_profiles.context: Qualified independent appliance technicians working with documented tools, safe isolation and a range of customer budgets.
stakeholder_profiles.primary_question: Can a qualified repairer discriminate likely faults and restore verified function without replacing unnecessary assemblies or repeating visits?
stakeholder_profiles.required_task_boundary: Qualified internal work remains subject to product-specific competence, isolation, stored-energy handling, guarding and post-repair checks; the profile cannot waive these requirements.

requirements.rationale: Travel, sourcing delays, diagnosis, hands-on work and verification all influence service time.
requirements.evidence_needed: Controlled scripts, timestamps, fault/task mix and exact tools/part IDs.

requirements.rationale: A repair counts only when relevant function and required checks are verified on the first visit.
requirements.evidence_needed: Documented task outcome, safe verification, participant qualification and denominator.

requirements.rationale: Service connectors and seals may add error and repeat work; the acceptable limit needs data.
requirements.evidence_needed: Repeated assembly/service trials and a declared event denominator.

requirements.rationale: Repair economics must include parts, labour, transport, failed attempts and rework.
requirements.evidence_needed: Dated part quotes/orders, labour assumptions and full repair receipts.

stakeholder_profiles.context: Independent parts suppliers, repair shops, distributors and local maintenance networks with finite inventory and cash flow.
stakeholder_profiles.primary_question: Can a lawful exact-fit part be identified and delivered within an economically sustainable service window?
stakeholder_profiles.required_task_boundary: Record lawful sourcing, model/revision compatibility, returns and supplier independence; a listing or verbal assurance is not a confirmed compatible supply path.

requirements.rationale: Delivery targets depend on market geography, customs, local stock and repair class.
requirements.evidence_needed: Dated accepted orders, exact-fit confirmation, dispatch and delivery receipt.

requirements.rationale: Dual sourcing and stock buffers can improve resilience but create working-capital and obsolescence burden.
requirements.evidence_needed: Supplier quotes, source independence, stock age, turnover and sensitivity model.

requirements.rationale: Elapsed outage includes parts sourcing; hands-on repair time alone hides supply failures.
requirements.evidence_needed: Start/stop timestamps, cancellations, substitutions, shipping and return times.

stakeholder_profiles.context: Lifecycle engineers, reuse/remanufacturing actors and stakeholders concerned with material demand, waste and useful product life.
stakeholder_profiles.primary_question: Does the architecture reduce whole-life resource/material burden while retaining useful function and repair longevity?
stakeholder_profiles.required_task_boundary: Only compare physically supported material, function and lifecycle evidence; no energy/water gain can offset safety or required function failure.

requirements.rationale: A smaller replaceable unit may reduce waste, but packaging, extra modules and failed repairs must also be considered.
requirements.evidence_needed: Measured mass balance for actual repair scope, discarded assemblies, reuse and returns.

requirements.rationale: Resource-use claims require the same validated useful output and uncertainty disclosure.
requirements.evidence_needed: Matched cycle tests with preregistered cleaning/rinsing/spin floors and instrument calibration.

requirements.rationale: Water use must be compared on successful function under declared incoming water and load conditions.
requirements.evidence_needed: Metered matched-cycle measurements and contextual assumptions.

requirements.rationale: Added modular interfaces can undermine lifecycle gains if they increase leakage, rework or failure.

stakeholder_profiles.context: Operators of laundries, schools, clinics, shelters, farms and remote sites where downtime and service logistics may be consequential.
stakeholder_profiles.primary_question: Can the appliance be safely and predictably restored when specialist service and spare parts are not immediately nearby?
stakeholder_profiles.required_task_boundary: The operator role does not imply technician competence; essential safe operation, local documentation and clear escalation remain required, and hazardous internals stay with qualified personnel.

requirements.rationale: Outage consequences vary by mission and backup capacity; no universal timeout is assumed.
requirements.evidence_needed: Scenario-specific owner/operator interview and elapsed-time logging from faults through verified return to service.

requirements.rationale: Remote operation depends on the right compatible parts being delivered, not on catalogue visibility.
requirements.evidence_needed: Exact-fit supply record, route/geography and dated delivery trials.

requirements.rationale: Repeat trips are costly where travel is long or service teams are scarce.
requirements.evidence_needed: Named remote service scenario, task and qualification profile, parts/tool readiness and post-repair proof.
